business_summary: Alphabet runs Google Services (Search, YouTube, subscriptions, devices), Google Cloud, and Other Bets such as autonomous transportation. Shared AI research sits at Alphabet level. In Q2 2026 revenue was $119.8 billion, up 24%, and Google Cloud grew 82% to $24.8 billion.
why_own: Alphabet combines high profitability and low FY25 leverage (operating margin 37.28%, ROE 35.7%) with accelerating revenue (Q2 2026 up 24%, Cloud up 82%). The case now also depends on very heavy AI capex and on reported profit that includes large unrealized investment gains, so headline net income is not a clean guide to operating earnings.

drivers.statement: Revenue keeps compounding at a double-digit rate (3-year CAGR currently 12.51%, versus 17.15% over 5 years).
Operating margin stays high (37.28% in FY25, up 6.05 pp over 3 years), so growth keeps converting into profit.
Returns on capital stay well above typical levels (ROCE 34.4%, ROE 35.7%) with little leverage (debt/equity 0.12x).
Reported profit is backed by cash: operating cash flow was 1.25 times net profit in FY25.

kill_criteria.description: Operating margin falls below 25%, well under the FY25 level of 37.28%.
ROCE falls below 15%, less than half the FY25 level of 34.4%.

risks.statement: Trailing-4-quarter net profit (244,205 USD m) is far above FY25 net profit (132,170 USD m). The Q2 2026 filing shows why in part: other income was $98.0 billion, including $99.0 billion of net gains on equity securities that were primarily unrealized (SpaceX and a private company), against operating income of $40.8 billion. Q1 2026 also had $37.7 billion of other income, mainly unrealized gains. The trailing P/E of 17.04x therefore rests on a profit base inflated by non-operating, unrealized gains, and no quarter in the last 4 was loss-making.

Capital intensity and financing are rising. Q2 2026 capex was $44.9 billion against operating cash flow of $39.1 billion, and 2026 capex was guided to $175 to $185 billion. In 2026 the company raised $49.6 billion from stock and mandatory convertible preferred and $20.3 billion of notes in Q2, plus $31.1 billion of notes in Q1. Long-term debt rose from $46.5 billion at end-2025 to $98.2 billion at June 2026, so the FY25 debt/equity of 0.12x and the cash conversion of 1.25x may not describe the current position.

Price/book is 10.02x, so the valuation depends on returns staying near current levels (ROE 35.7%). The own-history P/E comparison (32.3%) mixes a FY25 P/E with trailing profit that is 1.8x the fiscal year's, so it is not a clean read on whether the stock is cheap or dear against its history.
Legal and regulatory costs are recurring. A $5.2 billion EC fine (previously accrued) was paid in July 2026, and Q2 2026 included $2.1 billion of accrued charges from the PriceRunner decision.

The operating margin metric used for D2 and K1 (37.28% for FY25) is defined differently from the company's reported operating margin (32% for FY25, 34% in Q2 2026), so the two should not be compared directly. Rising depreciation from infrastructure spend and Alphabet-level AI costs (an operating loss of $5.8 billion in Q2 2026 versus $3.4 billion a year earlier) are pressures on margins.
Revenue growth over 3 years (12.51% a year) is below the 5-year rate (17.15% a year). Recent quarters are faster (Q2 2026 up 24%), but the evidence does not say how long that will last.

skeptic_counter_case: The thesis rests on FY25 ratios that the 2026 balance sheet has already overtaken. Q2 capex ($44.9B) exceeded operating cash flow ($39.1B). Long-term debt more than doubled to $98.2B, and $49.6B of equity was raised. The 1.25x cash conversion and 0.12x leverage are stale. The 17x P/E uses trailing profit of 1.85x FY25, inflated by unrealized gains. The thesis is wrong if capex-driven depreciation and a swollen capital base push operating margin and ROCE down, while the kill lines (25% and 15%) sit far below current levels and only trip after most of the damage. What would change this view: Seeing operating cash flow cover capex and interest on a trailing basis, with ROCE computed on post-raise 2026 capital staying above about 30%, would drop the objection.
